instruction: Access my Google Drive to download the invoice PDF, pull out the line items, and save them in an Excel spreadsheet on the desktop.

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting invoice PDF from Google Drive and converting to Excel on Desktop. Evaluator comprehensively verifies: (1) file exists on Desktop path, (2) file is .xlsx format, (3) proper structure with header and total rows, (4) exactly 7 line items extracted, (5) sample data content matches expected invoice items (laptop, mouse, etc.). Uses partial credit scoring.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: 0.2 for file on Desktop, 0.1 for .xlsx format, 0.2 for proper structure (header + total row), 0.3 for correct item count (7), 0.2 for data content verification (sample items match)

llm_judge_reasons: Complete verification coverage: Evaluator checks all critical aspects of the instruction (file location, format, structure, item count, and data content)
Desktop location verified: Getter checks '/Desktop/' in path (line 35) and metric awards 0.2 points for on_desktop=True (line 33)
File format verified: Getter checks .xlsx extension (line 36) and metric awards 0.1 points (line 37)
Structure verification: Getter validates header row (lines 61-66) and total row (lines 76-87), metric awards 0.2 points (line 41)
Item count verification: Getter counts line items excluding header/total (line 99), metric awards 0.3 points for exact match of 7 items (line 47)
Data content verification: Metric compares extracted sample items against expected invoice data (lines 52-76), checking Description, Quantity, Price fields with flexible matching
Partial credit scoring is logical and well-distributed: 0.2 (location) + 0.1 (format) + 0.2 (structure) + 0.3 (count) + 0.2 (content) = 1.0
Metric parameter handling is correct: directly accesses expected.get('item_count') and expected.get('sample_items'), proper handling of expected.type='rule'
Edge case handling: Metric checks for None/empty results, handles missing fields gracefully (lines 22-23)
Semantic flow is correct: Getter extracts RIGHT state (Desktop Excel with invoice data) → Metric compares RIGHT aspects (location, format, structure, count, content)
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Consider extracting more than 3 sample items (currently line 90 limits to 3) to strengthen content verification, though 3 samples is sufficient for most cases
Minor: Could add verification that header contains expected column names (e.g., 'Description', 'Quantity', 'Price') to ensure proper column structure
